analysis: The only changed file is CHANGELOG.md, a documentation-only patch that adds four 'Unreleased \u2014 demanded prefix reuse' bullets at the top (patch hunk at lines 1-11). No source code is supplied, so none of the described behavior could be verified. The described behaviors touch T-041 (prefix-cache sharing and the TTFT timing oracle, SEC-035) and the SSD write budget. Three claims are relevant: (1) a distinct demanded shared-prefix checkpoint is retained beside the deepest one, within the existing three-boundary limit; (2) authenticated repeated checkpoints get the reserved SSD write share on first local appearance; (3) one aligned demanded boundary is captured in eligible dense Qwen prompts below the solo stripe, which makes short repeated prefixes durable. Claim (3) may widen the at-rest and TTFT-oracle surface to shorter prefixes. The T-041 per-donation gating, which was based on the adoption bound and the 1,024-token benefit floor, may be loosened by it. The changelog states that the existing limits stay unchanged, but this cannot be confirmed without the Swift sources (SSDPrefixCache.donate, SSDPrefixCachePolicy, EngineV2Bridge) and the coordinator code. The next review pass should check that the source changes keep the HMAC lookup tags, the 30-minute TTL, the account-scoped cacheSalt and the disk budget intact. It should also check that the first-content budget reconciliation, which uses verified exact counts, cannot extend deadlines or bypass account/alias policy. The T-041 definition is still the one to consult. The changelog alone gives no evidence of a regression, so there are no findings. needs_deeper_review is set because the code behind these claims is not visible.
